neighbours.label: a determiner or quantifier where a drop, tear or other small bit of liquid (or of a plant) is expected next ('spill even one', 'shed a few', 'a tiny'); the same determiners outside a liquid setup stay low
fire: She squeezed the lemon until not even one more drop came out.
Add just a few drops of vanilla to the batter.
The old tap leaked a single drop every few seconds.
He wept quietly, shedding a few tears onto the letter.
In the heat, a tiny bead of sweat formed on his brow.
Don't waste even one drop of this expensive oil.
Morning dew hung in tiny droplets on the spider's web.
The nurse let a single drop of blood fall onto the test strip.
quiet: She checked the list until not even one more name was missing.
Add just a few pages of notes to the report.
The old clock chimed a single time every hour.
He worked quietly, writing a few lines onto the letter.
In the end, a tiny mistake formed the basis of the lawsuit.
Don't waste even one minute of this expensive meeting.
Morning traffic moved in tiny steps along the motorway.
The clerk let a single page of the file fall onto the desk.
